chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Isa ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who divorces his wife, then another man marries her after him, and she bears a child to the latter. Is the child of the latter permissible for marriage to the child of the first from a different woman? He said: Yes. And I asked him about a man who manumits his female slave, then another man marries her after him, and she bears a child to the latter. Is the child of the latter permissible for marriage to the child of the one who manumitted her? He said: Yes.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for the child of a woman's first husband to marry the child of her second husband?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the marital prohibitions of 'mahram' status are strictly limited to direct lineage and do not extend to the children of a woman from different husbands or masters. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that marriage barriers are based on consanguinity and specific fosterage, allowing intermarriage between the offspring of the first and second husbands, thereby facilitating social connectivity within extended family networks.
